title: Quantitative analysis of dense-core vesicle fusion in rodent CNS neurons
protocol: Start with a delay of 30 s to record baseline fluorescence.
Send 50, 1 ms pulses at 50 Hz to the stimulus isolator for 16 times with 0.5 s between bursts.
Add a delay of 26 s to record post-stimulus fusion events.
Send a 10 s pulse to the pinch valve controller to start superfusion of NH4Cl containing Tyrode’s 26 s after stimulation.
Incubate one coverslip containing uninfected DIV14 neurons with Fluo5-AM (2 μΜ final concentration) for 10 min at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Place the coverslip into an imaging chamber and add 500 μL of Tyrode’s solution.
Establish Tyrode's perfusion of 0.5 mL/min by placing one perfusion needle at one end and a suction needle at the opposite end of the imaging chamber.
Place two platinum electrodes connected to the stimulus isolator at opposite sides of an astrocyte microdot containing a single neuron.
Lower the electrodes as far as possible, just above the glass coverslip but do not touch the coverslip.
Make sure that the camera pixels are far from saturation since stimulation will typically induce a 100-fold increase in fluorescence.
Start time-lapse recording with image acquisition at 2Hz or higher.
Trigger the Master-8 via TTL pulse.
Repeat steps for a maximum of 5 times, or no longer than 1 hour.
Ensure to leave at least one astrocyte microdot between previously stimulated neurons and the next neuron.
Assess Ca2+ influx and efflux by plotting intensity over time of multiple regions of interests drawn on the neurites.
Place one coverslip containing DIV14 neurons infected with NPY-pHluorin into an imaging chamber.
Add 500 μL Tyrode's solution to the imaging chamber.
Establish perfusion and position platinum electrodes close to the neuron in focus.
Position glass capillary for Tyrode’s NH4Cl superfusion near the neuron in focus.
Start a time-lapse recording with Tyrode’s NH4Cl superfusion at the end of acquisition.
Install the DCV_pHluorin toolset by extracting the DCVpHluorin.zip file from Github into the Fiji.app/macros/toolsets folder.
Start Fiji and run the DCV_pHluorin toolset via selecting it in the toolset dropdown menu.
Open the “Option menu” to initialize the toolset after installation.
Install the “Check ROIs” plugin via Plugin > Install Plugin… in the Fiji interface.
Locate the “DCVpHlorin_CheckROIs.groovy” file in the Fiji.app/macros/toolsets/DCVpHluorin folder.
Open a time-lapse file in Fiji.
Manually inspect the file for focus drift, bleaching, and stage movements.
Open the ROI Manager.
Select “Fusion detection” under the “Start Analysis Menu.”
Set the movie normalization method to “Baseline subtraction” if images are noisy; otherwise, use “B&W Opening” as default.
Set the “Baseline frames” according to time-lapse acquisition settings.
Set the “Start of NH4 (frame)” according to time-lapse acquisition settings.
Select the “Number of stimulations” accordingly.
Set the “Stimulation time (in frames)” by rounding the duration of stimulation to the closest multiple of 10.
Adjust the “Smoothing radius” to improve signal difference between background and foreground.
Reduce scatter noise.
Enter the value for the “SNR” as a number between 0 and 255.
Select “Evaluate SNR.”
Run the Fiji “Find Maxima” function with “Preview point selection.”
Adjust the value of the “prominence” until the majority of puncta are selected without selecting background noise.
Close the “Find Maxima.”
Report the prominence value on the “Evaluate SNR” dialog.
Restart the program.
If the “Baseline subtraction” method was selected, insert a desired “Detection threshold” as number of standard deviations above the mean intensity signal.
Insert a desired “Cleaning threshold” as number of standard deviations above the mean intensity signal.
Adjust the “ROI size” to match the observed size of the DCV fusion events.
Set the “Maximum pxs overlap between ROIs” to be at most 1/3 of the total pixel area.
Evaluate the outcome of the detection by playing the time-lapse video.
Make sure that the “Show All” option in the ROI Manager is selected.
Add any missing regions with the “Place ROIs tool.”
Delete regions by Alt + clicking inside a ROI.
Evaluate each ROI intensity and detection via the “Check ROIs” option in the “ROIs Interaction Menu.”
Adjust the detected frame for DCV fusion events as needed.
Remove or add DCV fusion events based on evaluation.
Make sure that the ROI Manager is open and empty, without any selections on the image.
Select “Get NH4 pool” from the “Start Analysis Menu.”
An option dialog will appear with the same options as in step 15.
Duplicate the image and invert the gray values for synapse identification.
Perform a morphological opening by applying a minimum filter, a maximum filter, and a Gaussian blur filter of the same radius on the duplicated image.
Subtract the morphological opened image from the original image.
Threshold the result using the “Triangle” method from Fiji Auto threshold.
Manually inspect the synapse mask and delete any extra objects.
Collect all data via the “ROIs Frame readers Menu” and select “From Folder.”
Specify the baseline frames to calculate the baseline intensity level for DCV fusion duration.
Indicate the start of NH4Cl superfusion.
Optionally, calculate the “Synaptic location” of the fusion events.
Estimate the total amount of pHluorin-labeled DCVs (“Pool Estimation”).
Generate a table with one entry per single DCV fusion event.
Create a table with three estimations of the total DCV pool.
Organize time-lapse files and their ROI Manager files in one folder for better performance.
Place NH4Cl response csv files and associated ROI Manager files in another folder.
Store images of the synapse mask in a separate folder.
